subject: Renewal acceleration: voucher / co-term structure for Northstar Analytics
messages:
From: Jordan Liu <jordan@northstar.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — timeline & co-term asks

Hi Aditya,

Our renewal for the Core inference capacity is coming up in November, and procurement asked me to surface options early so we can decide whether to annualize, expand, or take a short-term bridge. Two asks from my side:

- Can you share a set of concrete renewal options with numbers (discounts / voucher sizes / proration examples)?
- We likely need to co-term to calendar year end (Dec 31) if we pursue an annual commit — what does that look like mid-quarter?

Tentative timelines: procurement will issue a PO by mid-September if we have pricing and a short amending SOW.

Thanks — would appreciate a short options memo and a 30-min sync if helpful.

Jordan
Sr. Infrastructure Product Manager
Northstar Analytics
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan@northstar.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — timeline & co-term asks

Jordan — thanks for the heads up. Attached is a short options memo (PDF) with three paths and worked examples. High level here so you can share with procurement quickly:

Option A — Accelerated Renewal (FastRenew)
- Immediate 12-month annual commit, billed monthly
- One-time acceleration voucher = 10% of first-year commit (applied as credit across Q1/Q2 invoices)
- Effective blended discount vs current list: ~8–10% depending on usage profile
- Co-term: we can align to Dec 31 by pro-rating the first invoice for the shortened initial term

Option B — Smoothing + Banding (SmoothRenew)
- 6-month staged uplift (start with current commit + 30% top-up)
- Quarterly banding and a 5% voucher applied over two quarters to offset onboarding spikes
- Designed for customers expecting mid-contract growth — keeps unit economics predictable

Option C — Incremental Annualize (Annualize-Light)
- No upfront voucher; commit to an annualized MRR that triggers lower per-token unit price after the annualize threshold
- We include a 2-month bridging credit if you need immediate capacity before the next invoice cycle

Attached: Northstar-Renewal-Options-20260830.pdf (one-pager with numbers and a worked example showing a $450k first-year commit).

Next steps I recommend: 30-min call this week to lock a preferred path and procurement requirements. If procurement wants a single PO, we can provide a short amendment + SOW with the proration math for co-term to Dec 31.

– Aditya
Aditya Rao

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — timeline & co-term asks

Looping in a quick operational perspective from CS:

- If Jordan expects bursts (spikes) during Q4 product launches, Option B with a prioritized burst bucket is safest — we can reserve a small burst pool that draws from the voucher before billing overage.
- For co-terming to Dec 31: we recommend an invoice phasing where the pro-rated period is credited up front and the remainder is invoiced monthly after Dec 31 to avoid a large single invoice.
- We can also offer a 2-month 'bridge' voucher (applied in full in the first billing cycle) if Northstar signs by Sep 15; that helps with procurement cadence.

Happy to join the call and walk the SLO/latency implications if helpful.

— Naomi
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: procure@northstar.ai
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — timeline & co-term asks

Aditya / Naomi,

Thanks for the options. A few procurement questions before we proceed:

1) Can you guarantee there will be no list price increase applied to the committed unit price for the first 12 months of the new term? We need price protection language in the amendment.
2) For co-terming to Dec 31: provide explicit proration calculation and an example invoice schedule we can attach to the PO.
3) We need a clear true-up cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether overage will be invoiced or drawn from the voucher.
4) Please confirm the voucher / credit will be non-refundable and only usable against usage/invoice lines (not professional services).

Attached are a couple of procurement clarifying questions in a short doc: Northstar-PO-questions-20260831.pdf.

Procurement would like to lock the PO by Sep 15 assuming the above language and an SOW. Can you provide a redline-friendly amendment by Sep 7?

Regards,
Northstar Procurement
procure@northstar.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan@northstar.ai>, procure@northstar.ai
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — timeline & co-term asks

Jordan / Procurement — quick consolidation and concrete proposal so you have something redline-ready:

Summary proposal (numbers are illustrative and in USD):
- First-year commit (annualized): $450,000
- Acceleration voucher: $45,000 (10% of first-year commit) applied as invoice credit across the first two monthly invoices OR reserved as a burst bucket that is consumed before overage billing (your choice).
- Effective blended discount vs current list: ~6% (conservative estimate accounting for expected usage profile).
- Price protection: list price for committed unit rates will be fixed for 12 months from effective date. Any list increases within that period will not affect your committed unit price.
- Co-terming: we will co-term to Dec 31. The first invoice will be pro-rated for the shortened initial period; example math attached in the PDF.
- True-up cadence: monthly true-up with any overage invoiced monthly unless it can be offset by the voucher/burst bucket. Overage granularity: per-token usage rounded to the nearest billing unit.
- Voucher rules: non-refundable; applies only to usage/invoice lines; not for professional services.

Attachments: updated one-pager (Northstar-Renewal-Options-20260830.pdf) with the worked examples and a sample amendment template we can drop into DocuSign. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NS-2026-0412.

If procurement is comfortable with the above language I will send an editable amendment by Sep 7. Suggested next step: sign-off on the voucher style (credit-on-invoice vs reserved burst bucket) and confirm whether you want the voucher applied over two or four billing periods.

Looking forward — can we lock a short call tomorrow morning to finalize?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
